Dearest Traveler,

Ise-Shima is the spiritual cradle of our ancient Shinto faith. Hidden within towering forests of sacred Japanese cryptomeria trees lies the Grand Shrine of Ise. For over two thousand years, this wooden sanctuary has been dismantled and rebuilt every twenty years, a perpetual symbol of renewal and impermanence.

Along the rugged coastline of the Shima Peninsula, the courageous Ama free-divers plunged into the cold depths without breathing equipment, searching for oysters and pearls. Ise-Shima teaches us the beauty of letting go and starting anew—rebuilding our spirits just as the sacred forest whispers to the sea.

With sacred light,
Kokoro of Ise-Shima
